questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Equation of a Trendline
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14010570/assets/f6cbd594db6ab2454844d744ce1b776c3f561c4a6295abb9222ad2416c9f9292.png)

Determine the equation of the trend line shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,8)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(8,5).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{5-8}{8-2} \\  & =\frac{-3}{6} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-\frac{1}{2}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-\frac{1}{2}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{1}{2}x+b \\ 8 & =-\frac{1}{2}(2)+b \\ 8 & =-1+b \\ 9 & =b \\ b & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-\frac{1}{2}x+9.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14010570/assets/da0836fa401981d7a0a254a136036a0ead7e3be8eefff5ef3fdfb31070759f0a.png)

Determine the equation of the trend line shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(1,3)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(5,8).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8-3}{5-1} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=\frac{5}{4}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=\frac{5}{4}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{5}{4}x+b \\ 3 & =\frac{5}{4}(1)+b \\ 3 & =\frac{5}{4}+b \\ 12 & =5+4b \\ 7 & =4b \\ b & =\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=\frac{5}{4}x+\frac{7}{4}.
$$

Estimate the slope of the trend line for the scatter plot above. Round your answer to the nearest $0.5.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14010570/assets/b50fd1636cc2e1bb9d150eaba9cc25a3ccedff77e607bf22853004332a7c4ddc.png)

It seems that the trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})≈(3,6)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})≈(5,3).$

Therefore, we estimate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{3-6}{5-3} \\  & =\frac{-3}{2} \\  & =-1.5\end{aligned}
$$
